notes: Restaurant's own WordPress site, menu split across 9 category subpages; address on site matches work list. 7 core Vietnamese sections (Appetizers, Pho Soups, Rice Vermicelli Dishes, Banh Mi Sandwiches, House Specialties, Special Rice Plates, Vietnamese Beverages) parsed cleanly via item-code format (114 items). The 'Chinese Dishes' subpage uses the same item-code format for its first 2 rows only (kept, 2 items); its third code (C-17) is a garbled bleed-over listing ~50 unrelated protein/size-choice dishes under one code with no reliable name/price pairing, so it was excluded entirely rather than guessed at. 'Side Orders & Vegetarian Dishes' (41 items) used a generic NAME-then-PRICE parser since it has no item codes; a handful of rows split a single dish across a size suffix (e.g. 'STEAMED VEGETABLE PLATE SM' / 'LG') because the regex requires an uppercase start - these were manually reunited with their dish name from the source page text (Steamed Vegetable Plate Small/Large, Bowl of Steamed Rice Small/Medium/Large, Tom Kha or Pho Thai Broth Small/Large Bowl, Chicken or Beef Broth Cup/Small/Large Bowl, and one garnish side dish whose leading words were lowercase and dropped by the parser). No price was invented in any case - only the dish-name prefix was recovered from the same source text. Cent endings cluster on .25/.55/.95 (a Vietnamese-menu convention, not delivery-platform markup); divisor sweep found no markup cluster. First-party own site, no delivery-platform cross-check available.

name: Breakfast Republic
notes: Restaurant's own site (breakfastrepublic.com/food-menu-web/) lists items with photos and descriptions but no prices anywhere. Used the location's white-label DoorDash-powered ordering storefront instead (custom.order.online, backed by DoorDash's cdn4dd.com/doordash-static infra); address embedded in the page (1570 Camino De La Reina, San Diego, CA 92108) matches the work list exactly. 6 real categories read (Playing Fare, Benedicts, Vegan, Gainz, Sides, Coffee); 'Merch' category (non-food) excluded; 'Most Ordered'/duplicate carousel copies deduped against their category item by name+price. Cent endings are irregular (no clean cluster on .00/.50/.95/.99); divisor sweep 1.00-1.35 found no single-factor markup match, but the page does carry DoorDash's standard fee-disclosure boilerplate ('menu prices may be higher than in-store'), so a mild delivery-platform premium can't be fully ruled out - hence medium rather than high confidence. Two Benedict dishes were unlabeled in the raw data and assigned to the 'Benedicts' section based on their own names ('Traditional Benedict', 'Jammin' Bennie') matching that existing category, not on invented data.
